extracted.intended_audience: general readers and naturalists interested in 19th-century travel, geography, and natural history
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for producing first‑person travel/naturalist narrative that combines precise scientific observation (navigation, geology, tides, specimens) with anecdote, landscape description, and notes on indigenous peoples and logistics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Give precise geographic coordinates and measurements
rubrics_metrics.description: Record specific positions and measurements (latitude, longitude, bearings, depths in fathoms) for places and features.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples in the text: 'The courthouse... is in latitude 32 degrees 55 minutes 50 seconds South and longitude 0 degrees 34 minutes 45 seconds East of Sydney.' Also record bearings, distances, and soundings (e.g., 'anchored in 3 1/4 fathoms'). Use exact figures so readers and navigators can relocate features; include leading marks and charted positions where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain scientific/technical causes and their social consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: When noting technical matters (e.g., magnetic variation, local attraction), explain how they arise and what practical or social effects follow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The chapter discusses 'laying down the boundaries by the magnetic north instead of by the true' and traces this to 'local attraction and the difficulty of finding needles that agree' and to legal disputes over boundaries. Tie technical explanation to real-world implications (e.g., litigation, land disputes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Blend personal anecdote with broader observation
rubrics_metrics.description: Interleave short anecdotes and humorous or dramatic incidents with the scientific and geographic narrative to engage the reader.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 'MIDNIGHT ALARM' and 'LUDICROUS SCENE' are examples: a vivid domestic anecdote (pumpkins rolling down stairs) is used to lighten technical narrative. Use clear scene-setting, dialogue or direct action, and a punchline or reflection to humanize the account.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe indigenous peoples' appearance, tools, language, and behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Record observations of native inhabitants: canoes, weapons, ornamentation, language samples, and reactions to Europeans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: description of Torres Strait natives (outrigger canoes, spears pointed with bone, pierced earlobes), noting repeated words ('toolic' meaning iron) and behavior on contact. Provide concrete artifacts and behaviors; include cautious interpretation but document what was seen.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide detailed natural history and specimen notes
rubrics_metrics.description: List and describe flora and fauna encountered, include distinguishing features, local names, and taxonomic remarks when possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text names species (e.g., Ptilinopus superbus, Haemipodius melinatus), notes egg counts and contrasts with similar species (quail laying 4 vs 14–15 eggs). Give colors, habits, abundance, and where specimens were obtained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compare observations to existing charts and correct where necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: Note discrepancies between present observations and published charts or previous reports; record corrections and practical navigational guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'both it and the coast are placed on the charts too much to the eastward.' Give corrected bearings, hazards (reefs, bars), and suggested routes or leading marks for safe passage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document methods, instruments, and procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Record the scientific procedures used (magnetic observations, rating chronometers, measuring meridian distances) and any changes in ship/party arrangements affecting work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author mentions 'rate the chronometers' and 'magnetic observations'—describe how and why these were done, record dates/times and personnel, and note any limitations or failures (e.g., local attraction absent on Magnetical Island).

rubrics_metrics.name: Record tidal and hydrological data quantitatively
rubrics_metrics.description: Report tidal timings, range, flood/ebb lengths, current directions and velocities, and peculiar tidal phenomena.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'singular phenomenon of the tides ebbing and flowing twelve hours,' 'length of both flood and ebb is twelve hours,' and current velocities ('velocity... increased to two knots'). Give times relative to lunar phases, local high/low water, and differences along reaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use footnotes and references for clarification and cross-reference
rubrics_metrics.description: Include footnotes to provide supplementary information, prior references, or navigational notes without interrupting the main narrative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The chapter uses footnotes for clarifying previous observations, giving leading marks, and noting related sketches. Employ footnotes for technical asides, citations (e.g., Flinders), and navigational precision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employ vivid sensory landscape and wildlife description
rubrics_metrics.description: Bring places to life with sensory detail: sounds, colors, textures, and movements of animals and plants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Passages such as 'the hum of insects, and sudden disturbance of rich-coloured parrots, screaming and fluttering' illustrate using sound and color. Use specific plant and animal names and sensory verbs to transport the reader.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record practical logistical observations relevant to voyages and settlement
rubrics_metrics.description: Note availability of fresh water, anchorages, supplies (wood, fish, turtles), shelter quality, and suitability for future expeditions or ports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text emphasizes Investigator Road as 'the only anchorage for vessels of all sizes' and documents wells dug and water supply. Include assessments of anchorage depth, shelter directions, and nearby resources useful for planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Connect discoveries to historical context and naming conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Relate present discoveries to earlier explorers and name features to record homage or continuity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author names the Flinders River as a tribute and records finding Flinders' ship-name cut on a tree. Use historical associations to enrich narrative and justify toponyms, and explain reasons for chosen names.
